faq_heading: Ocean Park homes: your questions answered

faq.q: Does Ocean Park have its own sold-price figures?
faq.a: Not from the board. Ocean Park shares MLS® sub-area F53 with Crescent Beach, so any sold figure for the sub-area describes both. This page does not try to split them.

faq.q: What does a house in Ocean Park cost?
faq.a: In F53 the median detached house sold for $1,740,000 over the year to November 6, 2026 (123 sales). Ocean Park and Crescent Beach are in that number together.

faq.q: Why might a home I know is in Ocean Park be missing from the search?
faq.a: The search finds listings that mention Ocean Park in their text. If the agent’s description does not use the name, the home will not show here, but it will appear in the Crescent Beach and Ocean Park search.

faq.q: What is there to do in Ocean Park?
faq.a: The Community Hall (1925), the Ocean Park Branch library, Kwomais Point Park and the Crescent Park Annex schoolhouse (1918) are the local landmarks, with Crescent Park, Ocean Cliff, Ray Shepherd and Laronde elementary schools nearby.

blocks.text: Draft for Jared’s approval. Sold figures are Jared’s Paragon pull of November 7, 2026 (closed and pending). The live search is connected.

Ocean Park is the settled residential community on the east side of Boundary Bay, in the southwest corner of South Surrey. The Multiple Listing Service files it with Crescent Beach under one sub-area, “Crescent Bch Ocean Pk.” (F53), so the board reports the two together. Near the water, coastal flood rules shape a home; up on the bluffs and the upland streets, slope and drainage do.

The search below picks up homes for sale in F53 whose listing text mentions Ocean Park. Listings are not tagged by neighbourhood inside the sub-area, so a home whose description leaves the name out will not appear, and one that mentions Ocean Park can sit closer to Crescent Beach. The Crescent Beach and Ocean Park search shows every home in both.

Sales here are reported with Crescent Beach, so the numbers describe both. From November 7, 2025 to November 6, 2026, 123 detached houses sold at a median of $1,740,000. In the most recent six months (May 7 to November 6, 2026) there were 62 sales at $1,656,500, a little under the full-year median. Townhomes (13 sales, $824,000) and condos (10 sales, $1,237,500) are small groups next to houses.
The typical house in these sales was built in 1986 on a lot of about 7,958 square feet, so a typical sale is an older house on a mid-sized lot.

blocks.text: Ocean Park landmarks and getting around

items.t: Ocean Park Community Hall, at 1577 128 Street, dates from 1925, and the Ocean Park Branch library, a 6,500 square foot branch, is at 12854 17 Avenue.
Crescent Park Annex, at 2378 124 Street, opened in 1918 and is described as the only one-room schoolhouse in Surrey still standing on its original site.
Kwomais Point Park, at 1367 128 Street, has a viewing platform over Semiahmoo Bay and a forest path between 126A and 128 Street.

blocks.text: Surrey Schools (SD36) elementary schools with addresses in the area include Crescent Park (2440 128 Street), Ocean Cliff (12550 20 Avenue), Ray Shepherd (1650 136 Street) and Laronde (1880 Laronde Drive). Elgin Park Secondary is at 13484 24 Avenue. Confirm the catchment with the district before you offer.

blocks.text: What to check on an Ocean Park home

items.t: On the older upland streets, look at the age of the house, the drainage and the lot width, and ask what the zone allows if you plan to rebuild or add on. A new house next door does not show what your lot allows.
On the slopes, look at retaining walls, stairs and where storm water goes, and ask whether a geotechnical report exists and whether the City holds slope notes for the lot.
If a tree on a slope needs to come out, ask whether a permit is required first.
